pages.text: All crops need to be planted on farmland in order to grow. Some crops have additional requirements such as being waterlogged or requiring a stick to grow on.$(br2)Crops do not need $(thing)nutrients$() to grow, but they certainly help. There are three nutrients: $(b)Nitrogen$(), $(6)Phosphorous$(), and $(d)Potassium$(). Each crop has a favorite nutrient.
pages.title: Growing Crops

pages.text: Consuming its favorite nutrient causes a crop to grow faster, and improves the yield of the crop at harvest time. That means that crops that consumed more nutrients drop more food when broken! Consuming a nutrient also has the effect of replenishing the other nutrients around it a small amount.$(br)Every crop has a different $(l:tfc:the_world/climate#temperature)Temperature$() and $(l:tfc:agriculture/growing_crops#hydration)Hydration$() requirement. You can find each crops climate range in $(l:tfc:the_world/wild_crops)[Wild Crops]$() or in its item tooltip.

When crops are planted without sufficient hydration or outside their temperature range the crop will die. If a crop reaches full maturity before dying it will yield excess seeds. You can kill a crop with $(l:tfc:agriculture/composting#rotten_compost)Rotten Compost$() to purposefully duplicate its seeds. Crops planted in $(l:tfc:agriculture/greenhouse)Greenhouse Planters$() are not capable of dying and will automatically provide bonus seeds.

Hydration is a measure of the % water available for the crop. Different crop types calculate their hydration differently.$(li)$(l:tfc:the_world/wild_crops)Crop$() and $(l:tfc:the_world/wild_fruits#tall_bushes)Berry Bush$() hydration is affected by both local rainfall and proximity to fresh water.$(li2)To be very specific you can calculate crop hydration by following: $(o)$(2)(60 * rainfall / $(t:500 is the maximum rainfall allowed. If you used configs to change the max rainfall replace 500 with that number.)500$()$(o)$(2)) + 20 * (5 - waterCost)$() where $(t:Distance from water is calculated as a 3D grid.)waterCost is the distance to fresh water from 1-5$()
pages.title: Hydration

pages.text: $(li)Hydration for $(l:tfc:the_world/wild_fruits#fruit_trees)Fruit Trees$(), $(l:tfc:the_world/wild_fruits#palm_fruit_trees)Palm Fruit Trees$(), and $(l:tfc:the_world/wild_fruits#banana)Bananas$() is calculated with: $(o)$(2)rainfall / 5$()$(br2)Grapes do not have a hydration requirement. Submerged crops like rice and cranberries also have no hydration requirement since... well... they are submerged in water.

Grapes must be grown on trellises constructed from posts and jute fiber. To construct a trellis, place two posts vertically. Then, leaving a one block gap construct another post to the left or right. $(item)$(k:key.use)$() the top and bottom posts with $(thing)Jute Fiber$() to string lines between the posts. Finally plant a grape seed in the space between the posts on dirt or soil. Grape trellises can be chained horizontally to create rows of grapes.
pages.title: Growing Grapes

pages.text: Provided the $(l:tfc:the_world/climate#temperature)Temperature$() requirements are satisfied, the grape vine will grow up and over the trellis over the course of a few months. It will fruit in the month of July, flowering the month prior. Grapes can then be harvested and used to produce $(l:tfc:cooking/alcohol#wine_making)Wine$().$(br2)Grape plants will not die even when they are outside their temperature range. But they will go dormant and won't produce any fruit until they are back to the right temperature.
